question: Do the covered observations jointly support a hypothesis of tighter readily deliverable copper conditions in China?
mechanism: A tighter nearby spread and falling visible inventory are modeled expectations of reduced readily deliverable supply. Rising domestic refined output can weaken that supply-side interpretation, all else equal. These are contestable associations, not identified causal effects.
alternative_explanations: Inventory moved between covered and uncovered locations rather than being consumed.
Publication lags and different observation frequencies obscure economic timing.
Contract-specific positioning or financing affected nearby spreads.
Customs revisions or reporting-definition changes altered comparable coverage.
Higher production coincided with stronger demand not measured by this fixture.
boundary: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION ONLY. All market values, contract identifiers, source names, and effective dates are invented test inputs. Evidence is conditional on the stated mechanism and source coverage. This does not establish actual China copper conditions, demand, causality, price forecasts, trading recommendations, or operational live-feed performance.

rules.name: Nearby spread
rules.rationale: Widening earlier-minus-later settlement spread conditionally supports tighter nearby availability; same contract pair required.

rules.name: Visible inventory
rules.rationale: Falling covered stocks support the hypothesis only if source definition and coverage are comparable.

rules.name: Refined production
rules.rationale: Higher domestic supply weakens this narrow supply-side mechanism, conditional on unchanged unobserved demand.

rules.name: Refined imports
rules.rationale: Import changes may reflect demand, arbitrage, timing, or substitution; direction alone cannot classify physical tightness.

rules.name: Shipments
rules.rationale: Optional contextual input; explicitly unavailable before local receipt, even if published earlier.
